subtitle: Find useful guidance when equity questions come up, keep formal responsibilities clear and build your own ability to examine equity in your daily work.
scope: For staff across DHS. Practice examples teach how to seek and use help; they do not resolve a complaint, approve an accommodation or authorize a policy change. Private reflection and invented examples are valid alternatives to actual work. Do not enter sensitive records into a learning activity. Actual requests and concerns follow the applicable agency process. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: An equity question may begin with uncertainty: a service route seems to leave someone out, a meeting favors one kind of contribution, or a proposed policy needs a fuller examination of its effects. Getting help is part of developing sound judgment. The important distinction is what kind of help the situation needs. Learning support, policy analysis, an accommodation request and a workplace complaint have different purposes and responsible roles. This course follows practice questions through those distinctions. You will practice a clear question, a proportionate description and a useful next step. Consultant guidance can strengthen your analysis while you continue doing the work. Formal requirements retain their own processes; a learning conversation does not replace them. You may use the cases at your own pace or reflect privately without recording a personal account.

intro.heading: Start with the question you need answered
intro.body:
An equity question does not have to arrive as a finished analysis. You may notice that a process is hard to use, wonder whose perspective a draft assumes, or need help comparing possible changes. Begin with the specific situation and the question you want answered. Separate the observation from a cause or motive you have not established. This gives a colleague something useful to examine without making them endorse a premature conclusion.

In a practice service-information review, Devon notices that a translated notice is an image-only file. A person using a screen reader says the file does not provide readable text. Devon knows about this file and that expressed difficulty. Devon does not yet know how often it occurs, whether other versions are usable or why the publishing process produced it. The first useful question is how the current information can be accessed and how the route should be examined.

Different questions can need parallel action. A person’s immediate request for usable information belongs with the appropriate service and access responsibilities. Devon’s broader analysis of the publication process may benefit from a colleague’s technical knowledge and consultant guidance. Neither should wait merely because the learning question remains unfinished. A consultation is not itself permission to change a formal requirement or a guarantee that a service barrier has been resolved.

For a learning exercise, use Devon’s case without names, records or private medical details from actual people. Privately examine an assumption about what a usable notice looks like if that is your purpose. In actual work, follow the appropriate information-handling and request procedures. You can ask which responsible role to contact without first gathering a personal history or proving the cause of the problem.

accordion.heading: Choose help that fits the question

items.title: Describe the actual difficulty
items.body: Devon can describe an image-only notice and the expressed screen-reader difficulty. This is clearer than saying that the whole program excludes everyone with a disability. The narrower statement preserves the concern and makes it possible to check the file, find a suitable route and consider whether a wider review is needed.

items.title: Keep the cause open
items.body: A publishing practice, a missing accessible version or another issue may explain the difficulty. Devon should not turn one report into a finding about motive or prevalence. Guidance can help choose the right evidence question; a formal determination remains with its responsible process.

items.title: Recognize a request alongside an analysis
items.body: Someone needs usable information now, while staff also examine the repeated publication process. These are connected tasks with different purposes. The broader investigation should not become a reason to withhold the appropriate response to the request. Use the actual service/access route and develop the analysis in parallel.

tabs.label: A vague conclusion
tabs.body: The program is inequitable gives little direction and may imply facts not yet examined. A useful description identifies the relevant file, the difficulty and the open question. You can keep the seriousness of the concern while avoiding a conclusion larger than the evidence.

tabs.label: An excessive personal account
tabs.body: Collecting a diagnosis or a private history may feel like making a stronger case, but the file question may not need that information. State the expressed access difficulty through its proper route. Ask the authorized role what information is relevant rather than gathering sensitive material for a learning conversation.

tabs.label: A clear initial question
tabs.body: How can the notice be made usable through the proper service process, and what publication practice should we examine? separates the immediate need from the wider inquiry. It allows specific help without treating consultation as approval or requiring a complete analysis before a request can be recognized.

check.question: Which question best starts Devon’s practice inquiry?
check.correct: Which appropriate route can address the expressed file difficulty, and what evidence is needed to examine the publication process?
wrong: Why is every person in the program deliberately excluding people?
Can I collect a complete medical history to prove the file needs attention?
Should the request wait until my entire analysis is finished?
check.feedbackCorrect: The question names the difficulty, separates request and inquiry, and keeps cause and responsibility open.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A motive claim exceeds the evidence. A medical history is not needed for this practice file inquiry and must not be collected through an improvised route. Finishing an analysis is not a general condition for recognizing an access request. Identify the appropriate response and examine the broader process separately.

intro.heading: Use consultation to strengthen your own analysis
intro.body:
Consultation can help you see a missing perspective, ask a better evidence question or compare alternatives. You do not need to know a tool’s name before asking for help. Explain the issue and where you are uncertain. Within One DSD People, Access and Culture, the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant provides program leadership, knowledge, guidance and feedback. The purpose includes building staff capability, rather than doing every task for staff or requiring all work to pass through a consultant.

Devon prepares a practice question about the image-only notice: which experiences should the publication review include, and how should different options be compared? A consultant can help Devon examine assumptions and identify a useful way to hear from affected people without demanding private disclosure. Devon still prepares the evidence, develops the options and carries out the appropriate next steps. Advice to consider an option does not itself approve its cost, timing or use.

Keep the formal Equity Policy responsibilities separate. The policy names Equity Directors and Equity Committees in implementation and provides for Equity Director advice when requested. It also requires the DHS toolkit or, in the specified circumstances, a customized tool developed in consultation with an Equity Director. A conversation with the program consultant is not automatic satisfaction of those requirements. Use the applicable policy and business-area process when the actual task needs them.

You may also seek guidance for personal learning: an assumption about what respectful questioning means, for example, can be worth examining without producing a work report. Keep that reflection private if you choose. For actual project advice, describe what help you want and what decision still belongs elsewhere. If a formal concern, access request or reporting duty arises, follow that process without waiting for optional learning support.

items.title: Do not confuse related roles
items.body: Program guidance and formal equity-policy responsibilities can support the same work, but they are not identical. items.title: Use feedback without surrendering judgment
items.body: A suggestion to compare an accessible translated file with another permitted route is an invitation to examine feasibility, effects and limits. Devon should not copy the suggestion as a decided outcome. Record the supported reasoning through the suitable work process and retain the responsible review or approval.

tabs.label: Transfer the whole task
tabs.body: Asking the consultant to do every analysis may leave staff without the skill the program is meant to build. Specialized help can be appropriate, but name the particular question and the part you will continue doing. Guidance supports capability; it does not turn staff work into a universal consultant assignment.

tabs.label: Treat advice as authorization
tabs.body: A helpful recommendation does not establish authority to change eligibility, spend funds or bypass required analysis. Follow the actual policy and decision process. When a suggestion needs a formal decision, make that next step visible instead of using the consultation as proof of approval.

tabs.label: Develop the work with guidance
tabs.body: Devon can use feedback to refine the affected-perspectives question, gather permitted evidence and compare options. The consultant’s contribution is specific, staff ownership remains and the actual decision role receives a more developed analysis. Personal inquiry can also remain private without requiring an operational result.

intro.heading: Distinguish learning support from workplace concerns
intro.body:
Staff can learn from an uncomfortable interaction, but an actual concern may also need the agency’s workplace process. Asking an equity question does not determine whether a policy was violated. It also does not require you to settle the concern informally before using an available reporting route. Keep learning, support and formal responsibilities clear so that guidance does not become a barrier to action.

In a team in this example meeting, a staff member reports repeated remarks ridiculing a colleague’s national origin. That is a protected-class concern to take seriously through the appropriate policy process; a course conversation cannot make the final finding. MMB Policy 1436 provides reporting routes such as a supervisor or manager, the agency Affirmative Action Officer and Human Resources. Employees and third parties are strongly encouraged to report. Managers and supervisors must immediately report allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to Human Resources or the agency Affirmative Action Officer, and follow agency procedures.

Policy 1432 addresses respectful communications and behavior outside its exclusions. It expressly separates concerns involving protected-class status or sexual harassment into the applicable policies. Informal assistance may be useful when suitable, and a formal complaint route remains available. Do not label every respectful disagreement a violation or route a national-origin concern solely as a general misunderstanding. Context and the applicable process matter.

You can seek personal support or learning guidance alongside the proper report. Do not delay required reporting while gathering an unofficial collection of statements or waiting for a consultant’s opinion. This does not prohibit an investigation assigned under actual agency procedures and authority. Protect against retaliation, use the appropriate channels and avoid promises that a consultation guarantees secrecy, an outcome or a particular finding. Use practice material here rather than entering an actual complaint into a learning activity.

items.title: Scope changes the next step
items.body: A disagreement about the wording of a draft may remain respectful, while repeated national-origin ridicule raises a protected-class concern. items.title: Do not impose a confrontation gate
items.body: A person may choose a reporting route without first confronting the person they are reporting. Help should not depend on obtaining an apology or proving personal courage. A suitable informal conversation and a formal complaint have different purposes; applicable reporting and agency procedures remain available.

items.title: Preserve assigned authority
items.body: A manager’s immediate HR/AAO reporting responsibility cannot be postponed for an optional equity consultation. After reporting, assigned investigation or corrective-action duties follow agency procedures. The lesson warns against an improvised investigation outside that role, not against carrying out work the agency has properly assigned.

tabs.label: Only discuss it in a course
tabs.body: A course can teach how to notice assumptions and respond respectfully, but it cannot receive or decide every formal workplace concern. An actual protected-class allegation needs the applicable process. Optional learning can support understanding after or alongside that action without replacing a required report.

tabs.label: Decide the allegation yourself
tabs.body: Declaring a violation or dismissing the report before the responsible process acts can exceed a staff member’s role. Take the concern seriously, describe relevant facts through proper channels and preserve assigned procedures. The course does not authorize independent findings, punishment or retaliation.

tabs.label: Use the process and suitable support
tabs.body: Report through an available applicable channel and follow your role’s responsibilities. Seek consultation for the learning or systemic-practice question if useful. This approach can address both a real concern and the broader work without requiring either an informal confrontation or a consultant’s permission to report.

check.feedbackCorrect: The response preserves the supervisor’s immediate reporting duty and the agency’s actual procedures.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Optional consultation cannot delay the immediate manager/supervisor HR or AAO report. Confrontation and an apology are not prerequisites. An independent improvised finding exceeds the course’s purpose and may exceed the role; investigations properly assigned under agency procedures remain valid responsibilities.

intro.heading: Recognize access requests and their responsible routes
intro.body:
An access issue can be part of equity work while also carrying a specific request process. An employee may need a change because of a medical condition; a service user may need appropriate language assistance; a team may need to examine the accessibility of a shared document. These questions can overlap in a project, but their responsibilities are not interchangeable. A general learning conversation cannot approve every request or supply every kind of assistance.

In a practice work exchange, Theo tells a supervisor that reading the required meeting document is difficult because of a medical condition and asks for a usable version. Policy 1433 does not require Theo to use the word ADA or a legal phrase for the request to be recognized. The recipient promptly forwards it to the appropriate decision maker and tells Theo who that is. The actual agency delegation matters; the course does not assign all decisions to a supervisor or promise automatic approval.

The supervisor can coordinate the work and consult the agency ADA Coordinator as appropriate. Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation from an applicant or employee seeking an accommodation. Where an appropriate medical-information request is necessary, that responsibility belongs to the agency ADA Coordinator. Agencies must not request or accept medical records as accommodation documentation. A diagnosis should not be collected in a learning activity or shared with coworkers to justify a change.

A different person asks for help understanding service information in another language. Use the appropriate current service and language-access route; DHS provides information and selected translated documents, not a guarantee that every version is available. Do not guess language preference from a name or treat the employment accommodation process as a universal service route. Address each expressed need and examine a shared publication problem through its responsible process, without replacing either actual request with optional consultation.

items.title: Recognition is not automatic approval
items.body: Theo’s request should be recognized and promptly forwarded; the appropriate process examines it. The recipient does not need a legal label to take the next step, and recognition does not decide which accommodation will be provided. Keep the request moving without promising an outcome the recipient cannot authorize.

items.title: Coordinate work without collecting medical detail
items.body: A supervisor may discuss the work barrier and coordinate through appropriate roles. A request for medical information or documentation is different. Policy 1433 assigns an appropriate such request to the ADA Coordinator and prohibits supervisor/manager collection; an entire medical record is not acceptable accommodation documentation.

items.title: Two improvements may be needed
items.body: A usable shared meeting document and an employee’s individual accommodation may support each other, but improving the shared file does not erase the request or authorize disclosure of its details. Similarly, a clearer English sentence does not replace an expressed language-assistance need. Identify which task each response addresses.

tabs.label: Demand the right phrase
tabs.body: Requiring Theo to say reasonable accommodation before acting can miss an ordinary-language request. The policy recognizes several forms of communication. Identify the request and promptly use the appropriate process rather than treating terminology as a gate to help.

tabs.label: Ask for a diagnosis at the desk
tabs.body: A supervisor’s desire to understand the difficulty does not authorize a medical-document demand. Discuss appropriate work information and involve the ADA Coordinator through the proper process. Do not use a coworker vote, public explanation or learning form to gather or validate a diagnosis.

tabs.label: Respond through the suitable route
tabs.body: Recognize Theo’s employment request, forward it and identify the decision maker. Separately address a service-language question through current relevant resources. This keeps help connected to the actual need while preserving authority, privacy and the difference between a request and a broader improvement.

check.question: Theo asks for a document change because of a medical condition. What should the supervisor do?

Announce the condition to the whole team and ask coworkers whether help is justified.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response recognizes ordinary-language notice, keeps the request moving and preserves the proper information and decision roles.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Special words are not required. Supervisors and managers must not solicit medical information or documentation from the requester, and agencies cannot request or accept medical records for this purpose. Public disclosure and a coworker vote are not the accommodation process. Use the appropriate role and protect the information.

intro.heading: Make a useful handoff with appropriate information
intro.body:
A useful handoff helps the next person understand the task. For a guidance request, describe the issue, why it matters, what you know, what remains uncertain and the kind of help you want. This is a suggested communication aid, not a required agency form or a promise that every request will receive the same response. The actual process may need its own information and timing.

Devon’s practice consultation description could say: a translated image-only notice was reported as unreadable by a screen-reader user; the review needs to compare usable information routes and examine the publication check. Devon can include an invented sample and ask for feedback on missing perspectives, evidence and options. A complete actual service record, personal history or complaint file is not necessary to teach that question. Do not assume that calling an attachment a learning example removes its sensitivity.

Actual formal processes are different. A complaint procedure may need relevant details and identities; an accommodation process may involve protected information through its proper role. Do not delete required evidence or disguise an actual report merely to fit a short learning summary. Use the authorized channel and ask the responsible role what information is appropriate. A learning activity should not become an unofficial duplicate file for those records.

After the handoff, identify what you will continue doing and what response you need from the other role. Devon may develop a draft comparison while seeking guidance, with the actual project decision still elsewhere. Do not invent a consultant deadline or assume that a sent request means a recommendation was accepted. For a private personal inquiry, no written request is necessary. You can reflect on the practice question without recording your own or another person’s account.

items.title: A formal file has a different purpose
items.body: Short learning examples should avoid sensitive details. That principle is not advice to omit relevant information from a required complaint or accommodation procedure. The appropriate role can explain what the actual process needs and how to handle it; do not copy the whole file into a separate learning record.

items.title: Make the expected response specific
items.body: Feedback on missing perspectives differs from permission to publish a notice. Ask for the former when that is the need, and preserve the actual project review for the latter. Devon should be able to name the next staff action even if the consultation identifies further questions instead of a final answer.

tabs.label: Send everything
tabs.body: An unorganized collection can obscure the question and expose information that the recipient does not need. More pages do not automatically produce better guidance. Choose a suitable description and permitted relevant material, distinguishing the consultation purpose from a formal record process.

tabs.label: Remove every important detail
tabs.body: A summary so vague that the recipient cannot identify the issue also limits help. In an actual formal process, withholding relevant required information can obstruct its work. Use the appropriate channel for that purpose rather than treating privacy as an instruction to erase the facts needed by an authorized role.

tabs.label: Share proportionately
tabs.body: For Devon’s practice guidance request, an invented file description, source limits and a question about option comparison are enough to start. In actual work, verify the appropriate channel and information needs. Explain the requested response and the separate decision so a handoff supports rather than replaces responsibility.

check.question: What belongs in Devon’s practice request for analysis guidance?
check.correct: A suitable invented description of the notice problem, the evidence and uncertainty, a question about options and the separate next responsibility.
wrong: Every actual service record and medical detail from the person affected.
No description of the problem because privacy forbids even invented examples.
A statement that sending the request has already approved the new notice.
check.feedbackCorrect: The request makes the guidance purpose clear, uses suitable material and keeps receipt separate from a decision.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A full record collection is not justified by this practice guidance question. Privacy does not prevent a nonsensitive example. Sending a request does not establish approval. Actual formal processes may need relevant details through their authorized channels; do not place them in a learning activity instead.

lessons.statement: Use the feedback, retain its limits and choose the next responsible step.

intro.heading: Use the response and continue building capability
intro.body:
A consultation is useful when its response helps you think or act more carefully. It may identify an assumption, suggest a source or explain why the current evidence cannot support a conclusion. Treat that as material for the next step rather than a verdict on your competence. Staff capability grows through examining a question, using feedback and continuing the work, not through transferring all responsibility or collecting a cultural rank.

In Devon’s practice review, the feedback recommends examining whether translated material and its accessible version can be used together. Devon develops that comparison, names what is still unknown and sends the proposed change through the actual project process. If an appropriate change is later made, record what was implemented through the proper work procedures. A revised file is an action; whether people can use the relevant route is a further question. No complaint recorded afterward does not by itself establish universal access.

Follow-through also means preserving the right responsibilities. A consultation response cannot close an actual workplace complaint, approve an accommodation or remove a required policy analysis. Those tasks retain their procedures and authorized roles. When guidance points to another process, clarify the appropriate next contact and purpose rather than assuming the consultant will own it. There is no invented response deadline or guarantee that one discussion resolves the whole issue.

For personal intercultural learning, the gain may be a more nuanced understanding of your own familiar meaning of respect, participation or responsibility. That insight can remain private and does not need an operational result to matter. Use a practice case if you prefer. An optional next inquiry can be worthwhile even when no written record is made. For actual work claims, keep evidence and uncertainty clear; for personal understanding, keep agency and the choice not to disclose.

flashcards.back: A response that can inform learning or work; it is not automatically a decision or result.
The relevant action actually carried out, subject to its appropriate authority and process.
What changed for the people or task, examined with suitable evidence and limits.
Developing your own questions, reasoning and practice with useful feedback rather than dependence on universal approval.

accordion.heading: Choose help that fits the question

items.title: Keep the gain specific
items.body: Devon’s option comparison now connects language and format instead of reviewing them only in isolation. This is a useful analysis improvement. It does not prove the new route works for every user or that a decision was approved. State the supported gain so the next question remains visible.

items.title: Missing evidence leaves an open question
items.body: A quiet complaint record does not show whether people received or could use the notice. The responsible review needs suitable evidence about the route. Do not manufacture a success or failure from absence; identify the evidence, authority and appropriate next review.

items.title: Personal learning needs no performance proof
items.body: A learner may privately notice that asking for help had felt like loss of competence, then consider guidance as part of responsible inquiry. That understanding is valuable without a written report, an IDI placement or a measured service effect. Keep any separate work-effect claim tied to its own evidence.

tabs.label: Count the meeting as resolution
tabs.body: A consultation held is an activity. It may be valuable, but it cannot by itself establish implementation or the result for people affected. Clarify what the response contributed and which task remains with staff, a project decision maker or another formal process.

tabs.label: Require total independence immediately
tabs.body: Using guidance does not mean someone has failed to become capable. Different questions need different expertise, and formal roles still have responsibilities. Aim for staff ownership and thoughtful use of support rather than a rule that competent staff never ask for help.

tabs.label: Continue with a clear purpose
tabs.body: Devon uses feedback to refine the comparison and keeps the actual project decision and effect review distinct. A learner can also continue private self-understanding without an operational output. Both paths preserve responsibility, evidence and agency rather than ranking people or creating universal consultation gates.

check.question: What can Devon conclude after consultation improves the option comparison?
check.correct: The analysis is more developed; actual decisions, implementation and effects retain their own processes and evidence, while staff continue the work.
wrong: Every service barrier is resolved because a meeting occurred.
No complaint proves the new information route is fully usable.
Staff are incapable if they need guidance again.
check.feedbackCorrect: The conclusion keeps the supported analysis gain, staff ownership and the remaining responsibilities clear.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A meeting is not a complete service result. Missing complaints cannot establish usability. Seeking further expertise does not itself show incapability. Use the feedback to improve the next inquiry, preserve formal roles and describe an actual effect only at the strength supported by evidence.

sections.heading: Choose the appropriate help
items: Seek optional program guidance for a specific question while continuing your work.
Preserve policy Equity Director, HR, Affirmative Action Officer and ADA Coordinator roles where applicable.

sections.heading: Make the next step useful
items: Share a proportionate description and the response you need through the proper channel.
Separate advice, receipt, approval, implementation and effect.
Keep unknown information open rather than declaring success from silence.
Choose another private inquiry, practice or responsible work step with guidance when useful.

sources.title: MMB HR/LR Policy 1432: Respectful workplace
sources.note: Scope excludes protected-class and sexual-harassment concerns. Provides informal assistance and formal complaint routes without requiring a private confrontation before a complaint.

sources.title: MMB HR/LR Policy 1436: Harassment and discrimination prohibited
sources.note: Reporting choices, immediate supervisor/manager HR or Affirmative Action Officer reporting, agency procedures and protection against retaliation.

sources.title: MMB HR/LR Policy 1433: ADA reasonable accommodation
sources.note: Recognizing and promptly forwarding employment requests, appropriate decision roles and the agency ADA Coordinator’s medical-information responsibilities. No DHS delegation is inferred from policy examples.
